question: A programme office is setting a policy for how much scrutiny Claude-generated work should receive. Which two factors raise the level of human review required? Select two.
options: A) The prompt that produced the output was long and included pasted background.
B) A large number of people would be affected if the output turned out to be wrong.
C) The action that follows from the output would be hard to undo once taken.
D) The output arrived in a document format the team has not used very often before.
E) The output was produced faster than the same work would have taken by hand.
correct_answers: B) A large number of people would be affected if the output turned out to be wrong.
C) The action that follows from the output would be hard to undo once taken.
explanations: Prompt length says nothing about consequence. A well-supplied prompt may even reduce risk, and it certainly does not raise the review bar by itself.
Correct. Blast radius is independent of reversibility: a mistake that is easy to correct can still reach many people before anyone notices it.
Correct. Low reversibility means an error cannot be quietly fixed later, so the check has to happen before the action rather than after it.
An unfamiliar file format is a practical inconvenience for the team, not a reason to apply more scrutiny to the content inside it.
Speed of production is not a risk factor. How long the work took has no bearing on what happens if the content is wrong.
